text:
Person: Please turn on the front camera and lock the side door. I'm leaving for work.
Assistant: I can do both. Which door is the side door, the one by the garage or the one in the laundry room?
Person: The laundry room, next to the washer.
Assistant: Got it. The laundry room door is locked and the front camera is on.
Person: Also, can you ring my phone if someone comes to the door?
Assistant: Yes. Should it ring for any motion, or only when someone presses the bell?
Person: Only the bell. The cat sets off the motion sensor far too well.
Assistant: Done. Your phone will ring only when the doorbell is pressed.

A translation app helps when you meet words you do not know. Say you are in a park in another country and a sign is written in a language you cannot read. You hold up your phone and ask, What does this sign say in English? The app reads it and tells you. People change a few things: the language, how polite the words sound, and how fast the voice speaks. They say things like, Say it again more slowly, or Use the polite form. A tired traveler may just say, Translate that for me. Learning new phrases is a bit like stirring a pot: a little each day, and the words slowly mix into your memory. Many people ask for one new phrase every morning and ask to hear it out loud.

Leo woke up and rolled over. A bird was singing outside the window, and he felt bored before the day had even started. 'Read my list,' he mumbled to his phone. The assistant read out four tasks: pay the water bill, call the dentist, buy bread, and wash the car. Leo yawned. 'Count them,' he said. 'You have four tasks today,' said the assistant. That felt like too many. 'Cut the car,' Leo said. The assistant took washing the car off the list and said three tasks were left. Leo smiled, stretched, and finally got out of bed.

Oscar woke up to his phone buzzing again. Every minute it shouted another alert about likes and new followers. He rubbed his eyes. 'Stop the like alerts, but don't turn off messages from my sister,' he said. The assistant asked if he wanted all the other notifications quiet too. 'No, just the likes,' said Oscar. 'I don't want a cheap little buzz every time someone taps a heart.' The assistant switched off the like notifications and left messages and comments on. The phone went quiet. Oscar lay back on his pillow and smiled. Now the only buzz would be from his sister, and he could sleep ten more minutes.

An automatic pet feeder is a small box that gives your pet food at the same times each day. It is useful when you are at work or away for a weekend. People often change how much food comes out and when. They say things like, Feed the dog at seven and five, or Give the cat a smaller portion at night. Some feeders record every meal, so you can ask, Did Biscuit eat this morning? If the dog spills crumbs on the rug, you might ask for a little less. You can also say, Pause feeding until tomorrow, when the vet says your pet should skip a meal.

Simon was at the beach with his friends, texting the assistant on his phone. His nose felt hot and tight. 'my face feels like it's burning,' he typed. The assistant guessed he needed sun cream and said the UV level would stay very high until four o'clock. It offered to remind him every hour to put more on. 'yes pls,' Simon typed. Just then a wave rushed in, and one sock fell out of his bag and floated away. His friends laughed. The water looked pretty in the sunlight, but Simon stayed under the umbrella. An hour later his phone buzzed with a message: Time for more sun cream.

Juliette sat at her messy desk with a cold coffee. 'Read me the top headlines and tell me who won the football match last night,' she said to her phone. The assistant read three headlines. One was about a new bridge, one was about a school fair, and one was about a storm out over the ocean. Then it said the home team had won two to one. Juliette smiled. The fans always paint their faces blue on match days, and she knew the streets would be loud at lunch. She thanked the assistant and went back to her emails.

Jonah woke up sticky and sleepy. The afternoon was humid and the fan was not helping. He picked up his phone and typed in a hurry: 'what chapter am i on in my bok'. The assistant checked his bookmark and said he had stopped at chapter eleven, on page one hundred and four. Jonah had planned to call his cousin at six, so he typed again: 'remind me to read at seven'. The assistant set a reminder for seven o'clock tonight. Jonah put the phone down, opened the window a little, and let the cooler air in.

Person: Did my parcel come today?
Assistant: Which parcel do you mean? I see two orders on the way.
Person: The one from the book shop. Sorry, no, I mean the shoes. The book shop one isn't due until Friday.
Assistant: Okay, the shoes. They show as delivered and left in the mailbox at 9:40.
Person: I just got off a night shift and I'm too tired to look. Was it paid for already?
Assistant: Yes, it was paid for on the website when you ordered.
Person: Could you flash the porch light when the mailbox opens next time?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't tell when the mailbox is opened. I can send you a message when a delivery is marked as delivered.
Person: That works. Please do that.
Assistant: Done. You will get a message for every delivery.

Ioana was ten, and her family was going camping for her birthday. She sat on the couch with a small cough and asked the tablet, 'Make a packing list and tell me if it will rain on Saturday.' The assistant made a list: tent, sleeping bag, torch, warm socks, and a water bottle. Then it said there would be no rain, only sunshine. Ioana clapped. 'Put a gold star next to the tent,' she joked. The assistant laughed and said it could not draw, but it added a note at the bottom: Bring birthday cake. They would celebrate by the fire. Ioana's cough already felt better.

Person: Is the front door locked?
Assistant: Yes, the front door is locked. The garage door is open, though.
Person: Oh dear. Shut it, please. No wait, I'm taking out the trash first. Shut it in ten minutes.
Assistant: Okay. The garage door will close in ten minutes. Do you want a beep before it moves?
Person: Yes, please. A sudden noise would be rude to the neighbors.
Assistant: A short beep will sound for five seconds first.
Person: Can you also unlock the back gate for my grandson?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't control the back gate. I can only lock and unlock the front door and the garage door.

Tendai was driving to a job interview and felt nervous. A hammer rattled in the toolbox on the back seat every time he turned a corner. 'Put on the news station,' he said. The assistant tuned in to ninety-four point five. 'No, wait, I want the music station instead,' he said. The assistant switched to a channel playing calm piano. Tendai breathed out slowly. At a red light he spotted a sign saying the road ahead was closed. 'Is there another way?' he asked. The assistant told him to turn left at the next corner. He arrived ten minutes early and still had time to sit quietly in the car.

A person wants to know whether this month's electricity bill is more than last month's, and wants the answer by text.
Is my power bill higher than last month?
Electricity: more or less than before?
Did the bill go up?
Compare this month's electricity bill with last month's.
I'm at the hair salon, so please text me if the electricity bill is double what it was in March.
Is the fancy new heater making my power bill bigger?
Tell me how much more I paid for electricity this month.
Could you check whether my electricity cost is half of what it was in winter, and let me know?

A person wants to write down a quick idea as a note.
Note this.
Jot that down.
Save a note.
Write this down: buy milk.
Make a note that my purse is in the blue bag.
Start a voice note, and beep when you're recording.
Note to self: bring an umbrella, it looks cloudy.
Can you please keep a note of the idea I just had? I'm afraid I will forget it by tomorrow.
Put a note on my phone: call Dad on Sunday.

Andre was folding tiny socks while his daughter watched a cartoon. The episode would end soon, and the washing machine was still running. 'Tell me when the wash is done and send me a message when the dryer finishes,' he said to the kitchen speaker. The speaker said the wash had eleven minutes left. It promised to call out when the machine stopped and to send a message when the dryer was done. Andre pulled a wide basket closer and started sorting shirts. There was a juice stain on his son's sleeve, so he asked for a stain tip. The speaker told him to rub it with cold water and a little soap.

Nimal was not good with technology. His daughter had left a small box on his bedside table, and he did not know how to use it. 'I want to sleep more than last night,' he said to the box. 'Wake me later than usual.' The box said, 'Your alarm was set for six. How much later?' Nimal frowned. 'Is half an hour enough?' 'You can say half an hour more, or an hour more,' said the box. 'Make it an hour more,' he said. The box moved the alarm to seven. Nimal felt calm. He hoped the good feeling would last all night, and that tonight he would have a deep sleep.

Rahul came home from the hospital after a long night. His stomach was empty, and his diet plan said no fried food. 'Find a salad place nearby and book a table for two at noon,' he told his phone. The assistant found a small cafe and said it had a table at noon. It also warned him that the cafe closed early on Sundays. Rahul nodded. 'Noon is fine.' The assistant booked it and sent him the address. Then he asked to see the menu. The cafe served soup, salad, and frozen yogurt. Rahul smiled, set an alarm for eleven, and went to bed.

Noah did not like phones. His grandson had shown him a big button for the assistant, and now Noah pressed it and said, 'Haircut Tuesday.' The assistant asked what time he liked. 'Morning,' said Noah. The assistant found a free slot at ten o'clock at the barber shop on Elm Street and booked it. It said the shop took a maximum of five customers an hour, so ten o'clock was the last place. Noah smiled. The barber always welcomed him with a warm towel and a friendly joke, and he used scissors, never a knife. Noah wrote Tuesday, ten o'clock on a piece of paper to be sure.

Oscar was seven, and he wanted his sunflowers to grow the tallest on the street. 'Water the garden in twenty minutes,' he told the garden assistant. 'The sprinklers will start at four fifteen,' it said. Oscar ran to the fence and painted a blue sign that said Sunflower Club. The sun was strong, and most of the leaves looked thirsty. 'How much sun do they need?' he asked. The assistant said sunflowers like six hours of sun and plenty of water. Oscar's grandma lived a mile away, so he asked the assistant to take a photo of the flowers and send it to her. She wrote back with three hearts.

Ahmed woke up and remembered that a parcel was coming. 'Where is my order?' he asked his phone. The assistant said the jacket had left the warehouse and was fifty miles away. 'It should arrive on Thursday afternoon, between two and four.' Ahmed groaned. The delivery window was short, only two hours, and he had hoped for sooner, because he wanted to wear the jacket to the cinema on Wednesday night. 'Can you forward the tracking details to my brother?' he asked. 'He is home all day.' The assistant sent the tracking link to his brother. Ahmed said thanks and went to make some tea.

Person: Excuse me, could you please start a timer for the chess game? My grandson and I like to play with a time limit, and I forget how long has passed.
Assistant: Of course. How many minutes should each player get?
Person: Ten minutes each, please.
Assistant: Done. Ten minutes for each player. Shall I tell you the current time left every few minutes?
Person: Yes, every two minutes. We play every Friday, and last week I lost because I did not hear the buzz. And could you wipe the old score from last week?
Assistant: I can clear the saved score. Do you want to erase all past scores or only last Friday's?
Person: Only last Friday's, please.
Assistant: Cleared. Good luck with the game!

Wiremu got home after a night shift, tired and hungry. The hall was dim, and a new camera was still sitting in its box by the door. He was too sleepy to install it. He grabbed an apple, because his diet plan said no biscuits, and typed in a hurry: 'turn on the hall ligth'. The assistant switched on the hall light at half brightness. Then Wiremu typed: 'remind me to put up the camera at five'. The assistant set the reminder for five o'clock that afternoon. Wiremu smiled, finished his apple, and went to bed with the door locked.

Sigrid was hosting a small party at home after work. The room was dark, and her hands were full of snack bowls. 'Play some jazz on the living room speaker,' she said. A moment later she added, 'No, sorry, play it in the kitchen too, not just the living room.' The assistant joined the two speakers together, so the jazz sounded the same in both rooms. 'Make it a bit quieter,' Sigrid said. The assistant lowered the volume. She had invited six friends, and the first one was already knocking. 'Turn on the hall light,' she said. The light came on, and she opened the door with a big smile.

A person wants the pool water to be warmer.
Heat the pool.
Make the pool warmer.
Turn up the water temperature, please.
It's too cold to swim.
The pool feels like ice. Can you warm it up?
Could you please raise the pool temperature to thirty degrees? My son has swimming practice this afternoon, and he gets cold easily.
I'm having a birthday party with cake by the pool on Saturday, so would you mind warming the water before the guests arrive?
Would you kindly make the water warmer? The light is dim out here and I can't read the gauge myself.

Jing was rushing to the bus stop when she remembered her friend's birthday. 'Days until Tuesday?' she asked her phone. 'Four days,' said the assistant. Jing nodded and kept walking. 'Message Lena.' The assistant asked what to say. 'Happy birthday, see you soon,' said Jing. The assistant sent the message right away. She wanted to buy a present, so she said, 'Find gifts.' The assistant showed her three shops that sold flowers and cards online. Jing picked a small plant and the bus arrived just as she paid. She jumped on, out of breath but happy.

Sofia ran a small shop on a busy road. One morning she looked up and saw that the digital sign over her door had gone black. 'The sign over my door is dead,' she told her phone. The assistant understood that she needed a repair and found two repair companies that were open tomorrow. 'Pick the cheaper one,' said Sofia. The assistant booked a visit at nine o'clock and said the coupon in her email would subtract ten dollars from the price. Sofia thanked it. She put a paper sign in the window that said Open, and then she went back to her customers.

A digital door lock is a lock you open with a code, a card, or your phone instead of a key. It keeps your home safe and lets your family in without keys. People change the code, the time the door locks by itself, and who is allowed in. They say things like, Lock the front door, or Turn on auto lock at night. If a friend visits, you can say, Give Maria a code for today only. Someone coming home late from the theater may ask, Is the door locked? Then the lock answers yes or no, and they can lock it from the street.

A person wants to know how cold it will get at night at their campsite, so they can decide whether to bring a thick blanket or a carpet for the tent floor.
How cold will it be tonight?
Night temperature at the campsite?
Will it be chilly in the hills after dark?
Will it fall below forty degrees tonight?
Should I pack a thick jacket or will it be warm enough?
Will it be warm enough to cook outside after the sun goes down?
Tell me the low for tonight in the hills, please.
I'm camping up high this weekend. Could you tell me how cold the nights will be?

Nathan came in from walking the dog with the leash still in his hand. The air in the apartment felt dry and a bit stuffy, and the windows by the sea left a salty dust on the sill. 'Turn on the purifier and open the vent in the baby's room,' he said. The assistant started the purifier and opened the vent. 'I like the air cooler at night,' Nathan added. The assistant lowered the room temperature by two degrees. A few minutes later the air smelled fresh. Nathan hung up the leash, washed his hands, and went to check on the baby.

A game timer keeps a board game fair. It counts down while a player thinks, and it buzzes when the time ends. People change how long each turn lasts and when the whole game should end. They say things like, Give each player two minutes, or Stop the game after thirty minutes. If a rule sounds weird, someone may ask, What is the rule for rolling a six? Some timers also keep score, so you can say, Add three points to Sam. Nobody argues about who is winning, which keeps the game calm and fun. Keep a can of juice by the board, and the game can go on all evening.

Nandi sat on the porch while her grandson did his homework. She had planned a bike ride, but she looked at the hill at the end of the street and sighed. 'This hill is too much for me today,' she said to the bike computer. The assistant understood. It found three small, flat routes near her house and ranked them from easiest to hardest. The easiest was the lake path, only five kilometers. 'That one,' said Nandi. The assistant saved the route and started the trip timer. She put on her helmet, waved to her grandson, and rolled slowly down the quiet street.

A person wants to hear about local events this weekend. It is their turn to pick the plan, and they like a medium-sized crowd.
What's on nearby this weekend?
Any local events on Saturday?
List the events near me and tell me which ones are free.
Is there a street fair or a market anywhere near us?
Is there anything fun within a few steps of my house this weekend?
Find me something medium-sized to go to with the kids, maybe a market, and tell me when it ends.
Could you please tell me what is happening around here on Sunday afternoon? I would like to take my mother out somewhere nice.

Tyre pressure is the amount of air inside each tyre. If there is too little air, the tyre goes soft, wears out quickly and uses more fuel. A loose valve cap can let air escape. A grandfather who drives to the shops every day should check the pressure about once a month. Many cars show the pressure on a screen. People ask, What is the pressure in my front tyres? or Remind me to check the air next week. When prices go up, drivers can't afford to waste fuel, so they say, Tell me when a tyre is low.

A word counter tells you how many words you have written. It is handy for school work, emails, and stories. A kid might have an essay of two hundred words, and the counter shows when to stop. People change the limit and what to count. They say things like, How long is my story? or Count the words in this paragraph. If the essay is not pretty yet, they say, Fix the spelling or Make this sentence shorter. On a computer you click a button to see the count, but with an assistant you can simply ask out loud and get the number back.

Alessandro finished his shift at the hospital at seven in the morning. He sat in his car on the forest road, too tired to cook. 'Order pizza,' he said to his phone. The assistant said, 'You have ordered the mushroom pizza several times. Same again?' 'Same,' said Alessandro. The assistant placed the order and said it would arrive in thirty minutes. He drove home and waited on the couch. Forty minutes passed, and the doorbell was still quiet. 'Call the driver,' he said. The assistant called, and the driver said he was two streets away. Soon the pizza was at the door, still warm.

Person: Pay my rent, please.
Assistant: Sure. How much should I pay?
Person: Two thousand, I think. I'm tired, and I only want to buy some pork on the way home.
Assistant: Your last payment was two thousand and fifty dollars. Which one is right?
Person: Two thousand and fifty. Thanks for catching that.
Assistant: Done. The rent is paid. Anything else?
Person: Can you zoom in on the receipt? The numbers are tiny.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't zoom the screen, but I can read it aloud: two thousand and fifty dollars to your landlord.
Person: Thanks. A message said I still owe money. Is that false?
Assistant: Yes, it looks false. All your bills are paid.

name: oven_belt_speed
does: Sets how fast the belt carries cookies through a bakery oven, so each batch bakes for the right time and does not go dark.
inputs: the kind of cookie, how hot the oven is, and how many minutes of baking you want
people say:
- Slow the cookie line down, they're coming out pale.
- These are coming out too dark.
- Make each batch bake for twelve minutes.
- The oven is hotter today, so let them go through faster.
- I'm switching to the thick cookies, so give them more time.

Warming up the car on a cold morning, or on a chilly evening, helps the engine and the windows. With an app you can start the engine before you leave the house. The heater melts the frost, and the car is warm when you sit down. People change the time and the heat. They say things like, Start my car in ten minutes, or Make it warmer inside. In the north, where winters are long, many drivers do this every day. While the engine warms up, some people dust the seats or clean the mirrors. On a hot day they ask for the opposite: Cool the car down before I get in.

name: reply_tone_helper
does: Rewrites an email reply so it sounds warm, polite and clear, and can add a blind copy to someone if you ask.
inputs: the email you are answering, the tone you want, and who to put in blind copy (optional)
people say:
- Make my reply sound friendlier.
- That email sounds too angry, soften it.
- Write back to Anna and keep it short but warm.
- Send a copy to my boss, but don't show it to Anna.
- Can you make this sound less rude?
- Say thanks politely and tell her I'll come on Tuesday.

name: pet_walk_planner
does: Plans a pet's walks for the day, such as a morning walk or a swim at the lake, and spaces them out so the animal gets several short walks.
inputs: the pet's name, how many walks you want, and the times you are free
people say:
- When should I take Rex out today?
- Plan some walks so the dog gets enough exercise.
- Is it too cold for the dog to swim today?
- The dog needs more walks, and I'm at work till six.
- Set up three outings for Luna, one early.

Janis opened her shop and felt strange: the town was quiet and nobody was on the street. Her pulse was still fast from running to work. She sat behind the counter, picked up her phone and typed in a hurry: 'put order flowrs at the top of my list'. The assistant moved the task to the top and said it was now her first job. Janis typed again: 'change the due time to noon'. The assistant changed it from five o'clock to twelve. She nodded, tied her apron, and called the flower supplier before the first customer walked in.

Odile had just moved to the city, and her baby slept in the stroller on the porch. She felt a little lost, so she asked the assistant for help. 'Remind me to feed Mila at three,' she said. A moment later she changed her mind. 'No, sorry, make it half past two.' The assistant set the reminder for two thirty. Odile also asked where the baby should nap on hot days. The assistant said a room on the north side of the house stays cooler. Odile smiled. At two thirty the phone chimed, and she carried Mila inside to feed her.

Person: I need to join the meeting but my screen is small.
Assistant: Which meeting? You have two today.
Person: The monthly one with Gerald.
Assistant: Okay, I joined the monthly meeting. Do you want the text bigger?
Person: Yes, make it twice as big. My screen has a crack and it's hard to read.
Assistant: Done. The text is twice as big.
Person: Please mute me while I eat. I am holding a fork.
Assistant: You are muted. Tell me when you want to speak again.

A person wants to be reminded to start their homework in an hour.
Remind me in an hour.
Homework reminder, one hour from now.
Set an alarm for an hour from now to start my homework.
Tell me to study after I bathe the dog, about an hour from now.
Don't let me forget my maths homework this evening. Nudge me in an hour.
Set a temporary alarm for an hour from now, just for tonight's homework.
I have a test tomorrow morning, so please ping me in an hour to open my books.

Sakura was cooking, and there was flour on both of her hands. Her phone lit up with a call, but she did not want to touch it. It was leaning on a jar at the height of her eyes. 'Don't answer, and don't read me any messages,' she said. 'Turn on do not disturb until the soup is ready.' The assistant switched on do not disturb. It asked how long the soup would take. 'Twenty minutes left,' said Sakura. The assistant said it would turn the setting off at the end of that time. Sakura went back to stirring in peace.

Person: Call Sam.
Assistant: Which Sam? Your son Sam or Sam the pharmacist?
Person: My son. His voice is tiny on this phone. Can you make it louder?
Assistant: I made the call volume louder. Is that better?
Person: Yes. My granddaughter is in fifth grade and she set this up for me. Remind pills.
Assistant: Which pills, and at what time?
Person: The white ones, at eight. Can you tell my neighbor I will lend him the ladder?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send messages for you yet. I can call him if you like.

A person wants the steps of a fast pasta recipe.
Pasta recipe?
Show me a fast pasta recipe.
How do I make spaghetti quickly?
Read me the steps for tomato pasta and tell me how long it cooks.
It's snowing outside, so what can I cook in twenty minutes?
My cousin is coming for dinner. Give me an easy pasta recipe, please.
Could you please walk me through a simple pasta dish step by step? I have never made one before.

name: flood_alert_checker
does: Checks whether a flood warning is active on your street and tells you when the water is expected to rise, so you can visit higher ground in time.
inputs: your street name and, if you wear one, the number on your alert band
people say:
- Is my street going to flood?
- The river is rising. Should I be worried?
- Is it safe to drive home? The road looks pretty wet.
- Is there a flood warning near me?
- Water is coming under the door, what do I do?
- Should I move my car to higher ground?

Mia was a retired teacher, and she was flying to see her sister. At the kitchen table she asked her tablet, 'Is my flight more than an hour late?' The assistant checked and said it was thirty minutes late, which was half as late as yesterday's flight. 'The gate is B12,' it added. Mia was relieved. She packed salty crackers in her bag for the trip. 'Will it be cold at the airport?' she asked. The assistant said the building was cool, and that her hands might freeze in the waiting area. Mia put a warm scarf on top. Her dog would stay with a neighbor for the week.

Knitting is a hobby where you make scarves and hats from yarn with two needles. Young and old people enjoy it because it is calm. A beginner may knit during breaks from homework. People keep track of rows and change the size or the pattern. They say things like, Count my rows, Make the scarf longer, or Text me the pattern. A helper can remember where you stopped, so you can ask, Where did I leave off? Then it tells you the row and the color. Some people also say, Remind me to knit for twenty minutes every evening, so the hobby becomes a happy habit.
